title: Web accessibility WCAG semantics keyboard focus ARIA and testing
concepts: Accessibility is a product quality that supports people with diverse sensory, motor, cognitive, speech, and learning needs across devices and assistive technologies.
Semantic HTML supplies browser and accessibility-tree meaning natively; ARIA supplements semantics when native HTML does not express the needed role or state.
WCAG gives testable technology-independent success criteria organized under four principles; conformance level and scope determine which criteria apply.
Keyboard focus, accessible naming, and predictable interaction are behavior contracts shared by sighted keyboard users and assistive technology users.
A robust accessibility review combines automated checks with keyboard, zoom, visual, screen-reader, and task-based manual evaluation.

items: Manual review against WCAG success criteria

Added nine success criteria: 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum), 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced), 2.4.13 Focus Appearance, 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), 3.2.6 Consistent Help, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry, 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum), and 3.3.9 Accessible Authentication (Enhanced).
Removed 4.1.1 Parsing from the active success criteria; it remains only for legacy policy interpretation.
Adds the image role as a synonym of img and adds comment, mark, and suggestion roles. The latest published WAI-ARIA 1.3 remains a Working Draft dated 2026-06-04 as checked 2026-11-17.
Adds image, comment, mark, suggestion, sectionfooter, and sectionheader roles; draft status means implementations can vary.
Adds aria-braillelabel, aria-brailleroledescription, aria-colindextext, aria-description, aria-rowindextext and other draft vocabulary changes; draft status means implementations can vary.
Adds the ariaNotify API with normal/high priority and a permissions-policy-controlled aria-notify feature; this is draft and not a stable baseline API.
Prohibits aria-hidden=true on document root elements in the draft; do not treat this draft-only constraint as a WAI-ARIA 1.2 Recommendation requirement.

accuracyFacts: WCAG 2.2 is a W3C Recommendation and extends WCAG 2.1 with nine success criteria; it removes 4.1.1 Parsing from active 2.2 conformance criteria. For policies, conformance level and scope still determine applicability.

The WCAG principles are Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust. WCAG success criteria are technology-independent and testable statements; techniques and understanding documents are informative guidance, not the normative criteria themselves.

WCAG 2.2 criterion 2.4.11 requires focused components not be entirely hidden by author-created content; 2.4.12 requires no part be hidden at AAA. 2.4.13 Focus Appearance is AAA and has specific size/contrast rules, not merely a visible-focus recommendation.

WCAG 2.2 criterion 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) is AA with a 24 by 24 CSS pixel minimum subject to defined exceptions; 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced) is AAA with a 44 by 44 CSS pixel target subject to different exceptions.
WCAG 2.2 criterion 1.4.12 Text Spacing requires no loss of content/function when users apply specified spacing overrides; it does not require authors to use those exact values as the default design.

WCAG 2.2 conformance is not established by an automated scan alone. Evaluation needs all applicable criteria at the claimed level and scope, representative pages/states, and manual checks where context or interaction determines compliance.

WAI-ARIA 1.2 is a Recommendation; WAI-ARIA 1.3 in the snapshot is a Working Draft. Draft-only roles, states, methods, and constraints must be labeled experimental and must not be presented as stable interoperable baseline features.

The WAI-ARIA 1.3 June 2026 draft adds sectionfooter/sectionheader roles, ariaNotify() on Element and Document with normal/high priority, an aria-notify Permissions Policy feature, and a restriction on aria-hidden=true at document roots. Support and draft text can change.

ARIA roles do not supply native keyboard interaction or repair poor semantics automatically. Prefer native HTML controls and semantics; custom ARIA widgets must implement their interaction, focus, states, and accessible names.

Abstract WAI-ARIA roles are part of the role inheritance model and are not author-assigned roles. Deprecated roles such as directory should not be taught as recommended replacements for native semantics.

Automated tools detect only some accessibility failures and can report false positives or miss contextual failures. Combine automation with keyboard, zoom/reflow, contrast, motion, screen-reader, accessibility-tree, and task-based manual review.

The latest published WAI-ARIA 1.3 document checked 2026-11-17 is still the 2026-06-04 Working Draft; ARIA 1.2 remains the Recommendation. The draft aria-notify Permissions Policy feature has a default allowlist of * but implementations can still be absent and policy can disable notifications.
